speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are here for chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort. To begin our evaluation, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and have you noticed any blood or mucus in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Irritable Bowel Syndrome with diarrhea-predominant features (IBS-D).

I understand your symptoms have been present for four months, relieved by defecation, and accompanied by urgency, mucus, and incomplete evacuation. While your camping trip is noted, the chronic nature and specific relief pattern are classic for IBS; however, to rule out other causes, I will request a stool study.

REQUEST TEST: Stool_Calprotectin and Stool_Culture
